Risk surface: every JSON string field ends generated R code: - parameter[].variable → used bare column name inside summarize() - statistics[].fun → used calc_fns[["..."]] key - statistics[].format.fun → - groups[].[] → used inside group_by() - Label fields (label) → interpolated R string literals Mitigations (required): Identifiers (variable, fun, values): validate ^[-Za-z.][-Za-z0-9._]*$ — rejects anything containing ), ;, spaces, etc. String literals (label, pattern): escape \ → \\ " → \" embedding double-quoted R strings. title: Getting Started with ksTable
text: ksTable reads declarative JSON table specification generates plain, human-readable dplyr/tidyr R script. Running script data produces formatted tibble ready rendering ksTFL. Key design principles: Declarative: describe want, compute . Plain-R output: generated script ordinary dplyr — paste console, step , save file. infrastructure: calc format functions resolved environment just like R function call. Isolated execution: intermediate objects (.raw, .long) stay private environment never pollute workspace.
code: JSON spec  →  kst_compile()  →  R script  →  eval()  →  tibble  →  ksTFL
